answer: Each agent must lock a stake before it can submit a bid, and the protocol caps how much influence one identity can buy until that stake has aged through several settlement rounds. A sybil attacker can still create names, but each name needs separately funded capital that remains at risk: provable fraud burns the stake, while honest participation earns fees slowly. Calling a trusted relay opal, zenith, or nectar changes nothing; multiplying identities ties up real funds and makes attacks costly.
